Rashi on Nedarim 46a:1:1.english: And both of them are prohibited from setting up a mill and an oven - To permanently install a mill and to raise chickens in that courtyard.

Rashi on Nedarim 46a:2:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן היה אחד מהם מודר הנאה על חבירו כופין את הנודר - שהדיר את חבירו, למכור את חלקו. אתאן לרבנן דאמרי אסורים ליכנס לחצר:
Rashi on Nedarim 46a:2:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "If one of them was prohibited by a vow from deriving benefit from his fellow ... we force the vower" - [meaning] the one who imposed the vow upon his fellow, "to sell his portion." We come to [the opinion of] the Rabbis, who say they are prohibited from entering the courtyard.

Rashi on Nedarim 46a:3:1.hebrew: היה אחד מן השוק מודר מן א' - מן השותפים, לא יכנס:
Rashi on Nedarim 46a:3:1.english: If one from the marketplace was prohibited by a vow from [deriving benefit from] one - [that is,] from the partners, he may not enter [the courtyard].

Rashi on Nedarim 46a:6:1.hebrew: בנדרו הוא דפליגי - היכא דנדרו שניהם זה מזה, דזה אמר לחבירו "קונם שאני נהנה לך" וזה אומר "קונם שאני נהנה לך", דעכשיו נדרו זה מזה ממש, והתם הוא דקא אסרי רבנן ליכנס לחצר, דאיהו עצמו קאסר עליה. אבל הדירו זה את זה, דכל אחד הדיר את חבירו ואמר "קונם שאתה נהנה לי", "קונם נכסי עליך", דתרוייהי אנוסים — דכל אחד אסר ליה חבריה שלא מדעתיה — התם מודו ליה רבנן לר' אליעזר, דזה נכנס לתוך שלו וזה נכנס לתוך שלו:
Rashi on Nedarim 46a:6:1.english: It is when they vowed that they disagree - [That is,] where both of them vowed [not to benefit] from each other, such that this one said to his fellow, "Konam that I benefit from you," and that one says, "Konam that I benefit from you," so that now they have literally vowed [to prohibit themselves] from each other; and it is there that the Rabbis forbid [them] to enter the courtyard, because he himself is prohibiting [it] upon himself. But [where] they vowed to prohibit one another, where each one prohibited his fellow and said, "Konam that you benefit from me," [or] "Konam my property upon you," so that both of them are under circumstances beyond their control — since his fellow prohibited each one without his consent — there the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Eliezer that this one enters into his own [property] and that one enters into his own [property].

Rashi on Nedarim 46a:6:2.hebrew: או דילמא אפילו בהדירו [זה את זה] נמי פליגי - דלא שנא אנוסין ול"ש רוצין:
Rashi on Nedarim 46a:6:2.english: Or perhaps even where they vowed to prohibit [one another], they also disagree - For there is no difference [whether they are] coerced, and there is no difference [whether they are] willing.

Rashi on Nedarim 46a:8:1.hebrew: ה"נ מסתברא - דבנדרו מיירי, ובנדרו הוא דפליגי, דקתני כופין את הנודר:
Rashi on Nedarim 46a:8:1.english: So too, it is reasonable - That [the Mishnah] is speaking of his own vow, and it is regarding his own vow that they disagree, as it teaches: "[The court] forces the one who took the vow."

Rashi on Nedarim 46a:8:2.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא דנדרו - שנדר שלא יהנה מחבירו, להכי כופין, דאיהו הוא דאסר אנפשיה:
Rashi on Nedarim 46a:8:2.english: Granted, if you say that he [himself] vowed - That he vowed not to derive benefit from his fellow; therefore [we] force [him to sell], for it is he who imposed the prohibition upon himself.

Rashi on Nedarim 46a:8:3.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת דהדירו חבירו אמאי כופין אותו - הא איהו לא פשע, דמינס אניס. אלא ודאי בנדרו פליגי:
Rashi on Nedarim 46a:8:3.english: But if you say that his fellow prohibited him [with a vow], why do they force him - For he was not at fault, since he was forced [beyond his control]; rather, they certainly disagree regarding [a case where] he himself vowed.

Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:1:1.hebrew: ושניהן אסורין להעמיד שם ריחים ותנור ולהעמיד שם תרנגולין - דבכל הכי יכולין למחות זה על זה בלא נדר, כדאמר בפרק חזקת הבתים (ב"ב נז:); הלכך אסור לעשות עתה בחצר כשנדר, דאם כן מהני ליה חבירו על שלא עיכב, דדוקא דריסת הרגל אינו יכול לעכב כל כמה דלא חלקו. וי"מ דכשהעמיד ריחים באים רוב עם לשם וממלא חלקו וחלק חבירו, וכן לגדל תרנגולין — דמתפשטין בכל החצר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:1:1.english: And they are both prohibited from setting up a mill or an oven there, or from keeping chickens there - For in all these [matters] they can protest against one another [even] without a vow, as it says in the chapter [entitled] Chezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 57b); therefore, it is forbidden to do [so] now in the courtyard when one has taken a vow, for if [he were permitted to do] so, his fellow would be benefiting him by not objecting, since specifically [regarding] treading on foot, he cannot object as long as they have not divided [the courtyard]. And some explain that when he sets up a mill, many people come there and it fills [both] his portion and his fellow's portion, and similarly [with] raising chickens — for they spread out throughout the entire courtyard.

Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:2:1.hebrew: היה אחד מהם מודר הנאה מחבירו - משום דבעי למתני "כופין כו'", דלא שייך למתני בשניהם מודרין. וכופין הנודר למכור חלקו, דחיישינן פן יעבור. אבל רישא דשניהם מודרין — אין כופין, משום דמנכר; אבל הכא, דאין אסור אלא האחד והשני מותר, דחיישינן שמא יכנס המודר כשיראה חבירו נכנס — ולכך כופין למודר. ותנא "שמא יכנס" קתני לה. ולרבי אליעזר, כיון דשניהם מותרין, למה כופין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:2:1.english: If one of them was prohibited by a vow from deriving benefit from the other - [The Mishnah states this case] because it wants to teach "[and] they force [him to sell]," etc., which is not applicable to teach [in the case] where both are prohibited by a vow. And they force the one who took the vow to sell his portion, because we are concerned lest he transgress. However, [in] the first clause, where both are prohibited by a vow, they do not force [them to sell], because it is noticeable; but here, where only the one is forbidden and the other is permitted, we are concerned lest the one prohibited by the vow enter when he sees his fellow entering — and therefore they force the one prohibited by the vow [to sell]. And the Tanna teaches it [due to the concern] "lest he enter." And according to Rabbi Eliezer, since both of them are permitted, why do they force [him to sell]?

Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:3:1.hebrew: היה אחד מן השוק - הך בבא לר"א איצטריך, [דהוה אמינא] דלא קא שרי ר"א אלא כשהחצר שלו דקמפסיד בדבר, אבל אחד מן השוק לא שרינן ולא סמכינן אברירה כיון שאינו מפסיד כלום, קמ"ל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:3:1.english: If someone from the marketplace - This clause is necessary according to Rabbi Eliezer [ben Yaakov], [as one might have thought] that Rabbi Eliezer only permits [entering] when the courtyard belongs to him, since he suffers a loss in the matter; whereas [for] someone from the marketplace, we do not permit [it] and do not rely on bereirah (retroactive designation), since he loses nothing. [Therefore, it] teaches us [that he is permitted to enter].

Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:4:1.hebrew: אם יש לו תפיסת יד למשכיר אסור - דעדיין הוא ברשותו, ומדידיה קמיתהני, כיון דגם אחר שהשכיר יש לו בה תפיסת יד. אבל כשאין לו בה תפיסת יד, יצאה כולה מרשותו ואין לו בה כלום, ואינו יכול ליאסר. ומכאן פסק ר״ת: מי שהשכיר בית ואח״כ אסרו עליו, דאין באיסורו כלום. ומיהו יש לי לדחות, דמיירי דאדריה סתמא דאין עליו תפיסת יד, ואין דעתו לאסור מה שהשכיר; אבל אם אסר בהדיא, מצי אסרה. וכ״מ בערכין (דף כא -): (כל) המשכיר בית לחבירו והקדישו, הדר בו מעל, ומעלה שכר להקדש. ועל ההיא נמי קשה מההיא דפרק אף על פי (כתובות דף נט:): שדה שמשכנתי לך לכשאפדנה תיקדש, דקדשה; משמע דקודם שפדאה לא קדשה. ויש לומר, דודאי מה שהבית שוה יותר מן השכירות קדוש, אבל כנגדו חולין, והוי שותפים המשכיר והמקדיש, לכך מעל; וההיא דאע״פ ה״ק: לכשאפדנה תיקדש כל השדה לגמרי. אי נמי יש לחלק: דודאי בהקדש גמור דאסר לכ״ע, דודאי מצי מקדיש המשכיר; ובשמעתין דקאמר מותר, מיירי שאסר בקונם בעלמא, ואלומי אלימי לשיעבודא דשוכר, כדאמר גבי שיעבודא דבעל; וההיא דאע״פ דאמר דלא קדשה עד שיפדנה, מיירי שאסר בקונם בעלמא, אבל אם הקדישה הקדש גמור, חל ההקדש אם שוה השדה יותר על החוב. ועוד יש לחלק: דודאי הך דפרק אע״פ מיירי בב״ח, כדתנן: מוסיף עוד דינר ופודה כל הנכסים הללו; אבל הך דערכין מיירי בשוכר, ומצי מקדיש משום דסופו לחזור אליו, אבל גבי חוב דלא תחזור לו לבסוף אם לא יפרע לו חובו, לא מצי מקדיש. ובירושלמי מחלק בההיא דערכין בין הקדים לו שכרו ללא הקדים לו שכרו, דודאי כשהקדים לו שכרו אינו של משכיר כלל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:4:1.english: If the lessor has a right of usage, it is forbidden - because it is still in his domain, and [the one prohibited by the vow] is deriving benefit from what is his, since even after he leased [it] out, he still has a right of usage in it. However, when he has no right of usage in it, it has left his domain completely and he has nothing in it, so he cannot forbid [it]. And from here Rabbeinu Tam ruled [regarding] one who leased out a house and afterward forbade it to him, that his prohibition has no effect at all. However, I can refute [this], [saying] that [the Mishnah] is dealing with a case where he vowed against him generally, where he has no right of usage [in it] and his intention is not to forbid what he leased out; but if he forbade [it] explicitly, he can forbid it. And so it is implied in Arachin (21a): "[Anyone] who leases a house to his fellow and [then] consecrates it — the one who dwells in it has committed me'ilah [misappropriation of consecrated property], and he pays rent to the Temple treasury." And regarding that [Mishnah in Arachin] as well, there is a difficulty from that [statement] in the chapter Af Al Pi (Ketubot 59b): "[If a man says to his wife regarding] a field that I mortgaged to you, 'When I redeem it, let it be consecrated,'" [the Gemara states] that it becomes consecrated; this implies that before he redeems it, it is not consecrated. And one can say that certainly whatever the house is worth beyond the rental [value] is consecrated, while [the portion] corresponding to it is non-sacred, and the lessor and the consecrator are partners; therefore he commits me'ilah. And that [passage] in Af Al Pi is saying thus: "When I redeem it, let the entire field be consecrated completely." Alternatively, one can distinguish [as follows]: Certainly in [the case of] full consecration [to the Temple], which forbids [the item] to everyone, the lessor can certainly consecrate [it]; whereas in our sugya, where it says "it is permitted," it is dealing with [a case] where he forbade [it] with a mere konam [vow], and they strengthened the lien of the lessee [so that a konam cannot override it], just as [the Gemara] says regarding the lien of a husband. And that [passage] in Af Al Pi, which says that it is not consecrated until he redeems it, is dealing with [a case] where he forbade [it] with a mere konam; but if he consecrated it [with] full consecration, the consecration takes effect if the field is worth more than the debt. And furthermore, one can distinguish [as follows]: Certainly that [case] in the chapter Af Al Pi is dealing with a creditor, as we learned in the Mishnah: "He adds another dinar and redeems all these properties"; whereas that [case] in Arachin is dealing with a lessee, and [the lessor] can consecrate [it] because it will ultimately return to him, whereas regarding a debt, where [the field] will not return to him in the end if he does not repay his debt, he cannot consecrate [it]. And in the [Talmud] Yerushalmi, it distinguishes regarding that [Mishnah] in Arachin between [a case where] he paid him his rent in advance and [a case where] he did not pay him his rent in advance — for certainly when he paid him his rent in advance, it does not belong to the lessor at all.

Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:6:1.hebrew: [בנדרו הוא דפליגי] - בנדר מעצמו, דכל אחד ואחד אסר נפשו שאמר "קונם שלא אהנה ממך", הלכך יש להחמיר וקנסו רבנן; אבל הדירו כל אחד חבירו ליהנות משלו, מודו ליה רבנן לר' אליעזר דכאנוסין דמו ולא מיתסרו דאית להו ברירה, [ובנדרו] קנסו אבל בהדירו לא קנסו. וצ"ע בהא דתנן: "האומר הריני עליך חרם ואת עלי — שניהם אסורים בדברים של אותה העיר", אלמא בהדירו נמי אסרו רבנן! ונראה דכיון שאמר "הרי אתה עלי חרם", קנסינן ליה גם על חבירו, דבכל מקום השוו חכמים מדותיהם ואסרו שניהם:
Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:6:1.english: [It is where they vowed that they disagree] - [This refers to] where each vowed on his own, as each one forbade himself by saying, "Konam that I will not derive benefit from you"; therefore, one must be stringent, and the Rabbis penalized [them]. But [where] each one prohibited his fellow from deriving benefit from his [property], the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Eliezer that they are considered like those under circumstances beyond their control and are not forbidden, since they have [the principle of] bereirah [retroactive clarification]; [thus, where they vowed on their own] they penalized [them], whereas where they prohibited [one another] they did not penalize [them]. And this requires further study in light of that which we learned in the Mishnah: "One who says, 'I am hereby cherem [forbidden] to you,' and [the other says,] 'And you [are cherem] to me,' both are forbidden in the things of that city" — thus [we see that] where they prohibited [one another] too, the Rabbis forbade [them]! And it appears that since he said, "You are hereby cherem to me," we penalize him regarding his fellow as well, for in every place the Sages equated their measures and forbade both of them.

Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:6:2.hebrew: או דילמא אפילו כשהדירו חבירו קנסו רבנן - אי נמי, לית להו ברירה. ומיהא בפ' שור שנגח את הפרה (בבא קמא דף נא:) אמר בהדיא דרבנן לית להו ברירה, וצריך למימר דלית להו הך סוגיא (אלא בת״ש: היה אחד מהם מודר ופליגי):
Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:6:2.english: Or perhaps even when his fellow prohibited him [by a vow], the Rabbis penalized [him] - Alternatively, they do not hold [of the principle] of bereirah [retroactive clarification]. However, in the chapter [entitled] Shor SheNagach Et HaParah (Bava Kamma 51b), [the Gemara] states explicitly that the Rabbis do not hold of bereirah, and one must say that they do not hold of this sugya (rather, [they hold like the proof in] "Come and hear": "If one of them was prohibited by a vow... and they disagree").

Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:7:1.hebrew: ת"ש היה אחד מהם מודר - משמע שחבירו הדירו, ואסרי רבנן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:7:1.english: Come and hear: [If] one of them was prohibited by a vow - [This] implies that his fellow vowed to prohibit him, and [yet] the Rabbis forbid [it].

Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:7:2.english: Teach: "one who vows" - [meaning] that he prohibited himself from [deriving benefit from] his fellow:

Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:8:1.english: "Granted, if you say [it speaks] of one who vowed, this is why it teaches '[the court] forces [him]'" - For [he is] negligent, having prohibited himself from [benefiting from] his fellow, and he could come to a stumbling block.

Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:8:2.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת שהדירו אמאי אמר כופין - דכופין הנודר היינו המודר; אמאי כופין המודר, דמאי חטא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 46a:8:2.english: But if you say that he prohibited him [with a vow], why did it say "we force" - For [the phrase] "we force the one who vowed" [hanoder] means the one prohibited by the vow [hamudar]; why [then] do we force the one prohibited by the vow, for what sin did he commit?

Tosafot on Nedarim 47a:1:1.english: If he died or sold it to another, it is permitted - Because he only intended to forbid [it] while it is [still] his.

Tosafot on Nedarim 47a:1:1-2.hebrew: מת או מכרו לאחר מותר - לפי שלא נתכוין לאסור אלא בעודו שלו: שדה זה שאני לוקח בית זו שאני נכנס והבית שלו מת או מכרו מהו - מי אמרי': כיון דדידיה הוא, אינו יכול לאסור אלא בעודו שלו; דנהי דתנן: "בית זה שאני נכנס" ומכרו, אסור — ה"מ כשמדיר עצמו מבית חבירו, דעתו לאוסרו עליו (שהרי אסרו עליו) כשאינו שלו. ומיבעיא לאבימי כשאמר בהדיא "בחייו ובמותו": ת"ש כו' — הכא לא דחי "שאני הכא דקאמר בחייו ובמותו" כדאמר לעיל, דהכא כי נמי אמר "בחייו ובמותו" מיבעיא ליה, משום דאין אדם אוסר דבר שברשותו לכשיצא מרשותו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 47a:1:1-2.english: [If] he died or sold it to another, it is permitted - Because he intended to forbid [it] only while it is his. "This field that I am buying," [or] "this house that I am entering" — and the house is his — [if] he died or sold it, what is [the law]? - Do we say [that] since it is his, he can forbid [it] only while it is his? For although we learned [in the Mishnah]: "[If he said,] 'This house that I am entering'" and [the owner] sold it, it is forbidden — that applies [only] when one vows [to prohibit] himself from his fellow's house, [for] his intention is to forbid it to himself (since he forbade it to himself) when it is not his. And Avimi's dilemma is when he explicitly said "in his lifetime and after his death." "Come and hear, etc." — Here [the Gemara] does not reject [the proof by saying], "Here it is different because he said 'in his lifetime and after his death,'" as it said above, because here even if he said "in his lifetime and after his death" it is a dilemma to him, since a person cannot forbid something in his possession for [the time] after it leaves his possession.
